key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion favor dense Fe-based amorphous coatings, while greater humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing detonation-spray parameters to limit porosity could improve the long-term corrosion resistance of coatings on Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Characterize droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and wear under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance gains or humidity ranges, and the reported wear behavior involves Si3N4 counterface balls.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
